mainTopic: Agents and deposits with הקדש money: the robe-and-cloak case, when a holder of deposited money commits מעילה, and a holy coin mixed into a purse.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה. An agent was sent with a gold דינר of הקדש money to buy a robe, but he bought a robe for three סלעים and a cloak for three. The תנא קמא says both men committed מעילה. רבי יהודה says the בעל הבית did not, because he got a small, poor robe. The גמרא tries to learn from this that an agent who does only part of his job still acts for the owner. The proof is pushed back by reading the case as a bargain, and the גמרא then explains רבי יהודה's complaint and supports it with a ברייתא about legumes, which רב פפא limits to a fixed-price market. A new משנה follows. It teaches when someone holding deposited הקדש money commits מעילה by spending it: a money changer, a בעל הבית, and a storekeeper, about whom רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree. It then rules on a holy פרוטה mixed into a purse, where רבי עקיבא and the חכמים disagree, except in the wording 'a פרוטה from this purse.' The גמרא brings two reports of ריש לקיש's challenge to that last ruling, and רבי יוחנן answers both the same way: the man meant that the last coin left in the purse would be the holy one.

steps.title: The agent bought a robe and a cloak: both are liable
steps.stepSummary: The agent spent half the money on the robe he was asked to buy and half on a cloak he was not asked to buy. The תנא קמא rules that both the בעל הבית and the agent committed מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The agent went and bought him a robe for three סלעים and a cloak for three סלעים. Both of them are liable for מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: We are at the end of a משנה about an agent who was told to buy a robe with הקדש money. He bought a robe and also a cloak, and the תנא קמא says both men are liable for מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The robe purchase did what the בעל הבית asked, so the agent's act counts as the owner's act and the בעל הבית is liable. The cloak purchase was the agent's own idea, so he is the one who misused that money. The money was split into two acts, one by each person.

keyTerms.meaning: A robe, the main garment the בעל הבית asked for
A cloak, the extra garment the agent bought on his own
Using הקדש property for personal use, which needs a קרבן and payment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the agent is liable for everything. The robe part counts as the בעל הבית's act, and only the cloak part is the agent's.

phrases.english: and he went and brought him a robe for three
phrases.notes: 'Three' means three סלעים. The whole gold דינר was worth six.

phrases.english: and a cloak for three
both of them are liable for misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's case from before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the agent buys the requested robe with half and an unrequested cloak with half, the בעל הבית and the agent each committed מעילה.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the homeowner is not liable
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה disagrees and says the בעל הבית did not commit מעילה, because he wanted a big robe and got a small, poor one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: the בעל הבית is not liable, because he can tell the agent, 'I wanted a big robe, and you brought me a small, poor one.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה argues on the תנא קמא and frees the בעל הבית from מעילה. In his view the agent did not really do what he was sent to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The בעל הבית gave enough money for a big robe. A robe that cost only half is a different thing from what he asked for, so the agent left his job and the purchase is not the owner's act. This detail, 'small and poor,' becomes the key to the גמרא's later challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: The homeowner who sent the agent

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת לֹא מָעַל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: the homeowner is not liable for misuse,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר לוֹ: חָלוּק גָּדוֹל הָיִיתִי מְבַקֵּשׁ,
phrases.english: for he says to him: I wanted a large robe,
and you brought me a small and poor one.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת לֹא מָעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the תנא קמא's ruling about the בעל הבית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בעל הבית is not liable, since the cheap robe was not what he sent the agent to buy.
steps.whyThisMatters: The words 'small and poor' are used later by the גמרא to knock down the answer that the agent got a bargain.

steps.title: Learning from the משנה that a partly done job still counts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wants to prove from the תנא קמא that if an agent was told to sell a whole כור of land and sold only half, the buyer still owns that half.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא says: we can learn from here that if someone tells his agent, 'Go sell a כור of land for me,' and the agent sells only half a כור, the buyer acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a proof. It uses the תנא קמא's ruling to settle a question about an agent who does only part of what he was told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The agent spent only half the money on the robe, yet the תנא קמא treats that half as the owner's act. So doing part of the job still counts as the agent's mission. The same should be true for selling half the land.

keyTerms.meaning: You can learn from it, a proof from the source
A כור of land, a field measured by how much seed it takes

phrases.english: GEMARA: Learn from it:
one who said to his agent:
'Go sell for me a kor of land,'
and he went and sold for him a half-kor,
the buyer acquires!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule about agents from the תנא קמא's ruling
steps.raayaObject: An agent who sells half a כור of land instead of a full כור: the sale is valid
steps.raayaSupportSource: The תנא קמא in the משנה, who holds the בעל הבית liable even though only half the money went to the robe

steps.title: Pushback: maybe the agent found a bargain
steps.stepSummary: Others reject the proof. The משנה may be talking about an agent who bought a robe worth six סלעים for only three.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: what case is this? It is where the agent brought him a robe worth six for the price of three.
steps.whatsHappening: Some חכמים push back on the proof. They say the משנה might be a special case where the agent got a full-value robe at half price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the robe was worth six, the בעל הבית got exactly what he wanted, and nothing of his request was left undone. The cloak was just an extra. That is not like selling only half the land, so the proof fails.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?

phrases.english: They say: here, what are the circumstances?
Such as where he brought him
one worth six for three.
phrases.notes: A robe worth six סלעים, the full value of the gold דינר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof from step 3 by redefining the case
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof, not the rule itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the agent did only half the job. If the robe was worth the full amount, the job was fully done.

steps.title: Challenge from רבי יהודה's words: the robe was small and poor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the bargain answer. רבי יהודה says the robe was small and poor, so it cannot have been worth six.
steps.simpleTranslation: Look at the end of the משנה: רבי יהודה says the בעל הבית is not liable, because he can say, 'I wanted a big robe, and you brought me a small, poor robe.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer in step 4 by quoting רבי יהודה's words from the end of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the robe were really worth six, the בעל הבית could not complain that it was small and poor. So the משנה must be about a cheap robe worth only three. That brings back the original proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Look at the end of the same source
He can say to him, he has a valid complaint

phrases.english: Say the latter clause:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: בַּעַל הַבַּיִת לֹא מָעַל,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: the homeowner is not liable for misuse,
for he can say to him:
'I wanted a large robe,
and you brought me a small and poor robe'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the bargain answer in step 4 from the wording of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה is about a robe worth six bought for three
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה calls the robe small and poor, so the משנה is about a cheap robe, not a bargain.

steps.title: Small and poor compared to what he could have gotten
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's words fit the bargain case. The owner can say: had you spent the whole דינר at that cheap merchant, you would have brought me a robe worth two דינרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The owner could say to the agent: If you had given the whole דינר, you would have brought me a robe worth two דינרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 5. 'Small and poor' does not mean the robe was cheap junk. It means it was small compared to what the full money could have bought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that a 'small, poor' robe cannot be worth six. The answer: it really is worth six, but the agent found a merchant selling at half price. Spending everything there would have brought a robe worth double. So the owner lost out, and the bargain reading of the משנה still works.

keyTerms.meaning: A coin; here, the money the agent was given

phrases.english: That he can say to him:
phrases.notes: 'He' is the בעל הבית, speaking to the agent.

phrases.english: If you had given the whole dinar,
you would have brought me a robe worth two dinars.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר לֵיהּ: אִי יָהֲבַתְּ דִּינָר כּוּלֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 5 by reinterpreting 'small and poor' as relative.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Small and poor' means the robe was really worth little, so it cannot be the six-for-three bargain case.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Small and poor' is relative. With the whole dinar at that bargain price, the owner would have gotten a robe worth twice as much.

steps.title: Support from רבי יהודה agreeing about legumes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says רבי יהודה agrees that both committed מעילה with legumes, because legumes always cost the same rate whether you buy a little or a lot.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, since the later part teaches: רבי יהודה agrees about legumes that both committed מעילה, because legumes sell for a פרוטה and legumes sell for a דינר at the same rate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for the answer in Step 6. In a case of legumes, רבי יהודה agrees with the תנא קמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Legumes cost the same rate in small or large amounts, so buying half did not make the owner lose anything. That is why רבי יהודה agrees there. This shows his reason in the robe case is about losing a better deal, which matches Step 6.

keyTerms.meaning: This also stands to reason (supporting proof)
The later clause of a teaching

phrases.english: This too stands to reason,
as it teaches in the later clause:
phrases.notes: This later clause is from a ברייתא, not from our משנה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda agrees regarding legumes
that both of them committed misuse,
because legumes are sold for a peruta
and legumes are sold for a dinar.
phrases.notes: He means the price stays the same per amount, so buying more brings no discount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of Step 6 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's reason is the lost chance for a better deal, not the robe's poor quality.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's later clause: רבי יהודה agrees about legumes, since their price rate never changes.

steps.title: Don't legumes also get cheaper in bulk?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: in a place where things are sold by estimate, a big purchase of legumes should also get a discount.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it is in a place where they sell by estimate, then with legumes too, when someone pays a סלע, they give it to him cheaper!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא from Step 7. Why should legumes be different from a robe?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 depended on legumes always having the same rate. But where sellers price by estimate, a buyer who spends a lot usually gets a lower price. Then buying only half would cause a loss with legumes too, and רבי יהודה should not agree.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? (asks for the exact situation)

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If it is in a place where they sell by estimate,
then with legumes too,
when one gives a sela, they make it cheaper for him!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִי בְּאַתְרָא דְּזָבְנִי בְּשׁוּמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the legume case brought as support in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that legumes have a fixed price rate.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Where goods are sold by estimate, bulk buyers get discounts, so legumes would be like the robe.

steps.title: רב פפא: a place where each container has a fixed price
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the ברייתא is talking about a place where legumes are sold by containers, each container for a פרוטה, so the price is fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is a place where they sell by containers, each container for a פרוטה, because there the price is fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge from Step 8 by explaining which kind of place the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this place, every container costs exactly one פרוטה, no matter how many you buy. Buying half the legumes loses nothing, so רבי יהודה agrees that both committed מעילה. The support for Step 6 stands.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה exempts the owner only when buying less caused him a real loss of value. When the price is fixed, as with legumes sold by containers, he agrees that both committed מעילה.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It is in a place where they sell by containers,
each and every container for a peruta,
for there their matter is fixed.
phrases.notes: He means the price is set. Buying more does not get you a discount.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בְּדוּכְתָּא דִּמְזַבְּנִי בְּכַנֵּי כַּנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8 by limiting the ברייתא to a fixed-price market.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case to a specific situation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Legumes are sold by estimate, so bulk buying would be cheaper.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא speaks of a place where each container costs one פרוטה, so the price never changes.

steps.title: Using deposited money: money changer versus בעל הבית
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a money changer may not use deposited money that is tied up, but may use untied money. A בעל הבית may never use it. Spending money he was not allowed to use makes him guilty of מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who deposits money with a money changer: if it is tied up, he may not use it, so if he spends it he committed מעילה. If it is untied, he may use it, so if he spends it he did not commit מעילה. With a בעל הבית, either way he may not use it, so if he spends it he committed מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It asks when someone holding deposited money commits מעילה by spending it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything depends on whether the holder was allowed to use the money. Untied money given to a money changer is understood as permission to use it, because money changers deal in money all day. A בעל הבית is never assumed to have permission, so spending is always מעילה for him.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (start of a new משנה)
One who deposits (leaves something for safekeeping)
Tied up, bound in a bundle

steps.confusionAlert: Here מוּתָּרִין means 'untied,' not 'permitted.' Tying the coins up shows the owner does not want them used.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who deposits money with a money changer,
phrases.notes: The money is הקדש money. That is why spending it can be מעילה.

phrases.english: if it is bound, he may not use it.
Therefore, if he spent it, he committed misuse.
If it is unbound, he may use it.
Therefore, if he spent it, he did not commit misuse.
With a homeowner,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ לֹא יִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ בָּהֶן.
phrases.english: whether this way or that way, he may not use it.
Therefore, if he spent it, he committed misuse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic: deposited הקדש money.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A holder commits מעילה by spending deposited money only if he was not allowed to use it. A money changer may use untied money but not tied money. A בעל הבית may never use it.

steps.title: Is a storekeeper like a בעל הבית or a money changer?
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר says a storekeeper is like a בעל הבית, who may never use the money. רבי יהודה says he is like a money changer.
steps.simpleTranslation: A storekeeper is like a בעל הבית; these are the words of רבי מאיר. רבי יהודה says: He is like a money changer.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת about a storekeeper, who falls between the two cases above.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי מאיר, a storekeeper may not use deposited money even if it is untied, so spending it is always מעילה. According to רבי יהודה, he follows the money changer rule: tied money may not be used, but untied money may.
steps.whatToRemember: Money changer: tied money may not be used, untied money may. בעל הבית: never. Storekeeper: like a בעל הבית according to רבי מאיר, like a money changer according to רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: A storekeeper is like a homeowner;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yehuda says: He is like a money changer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַחֶנְווֹנִי – כְּבַעַל הַבַּיִת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the two categories of Step 10 to a storekeeper, with a מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: a storekeeper follows the בעל הבית rule. רבי יהודה: a storekeeper follows the money changer rule.

steps.title: A consecrated coin mixed into a purse
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: a consecrated פרוטה is mixed into a purse. רבי עקיבא says spending the first coin already counts as מעילה. The חכמים say there is no מעילה until the whole purse is spent.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a consecrated פרוטה fell into someone's purse, or he said 'a פרוטה in this purse is הקדש,' then once he spends the first coin he is guilty of מעילה. These are the words of רבי עקיבא. The חכמים say he is not guilty until he spends the entire purse.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins a new case. A holy coin is mixed in with ordinary coins, and רבי עקיבא and the חכמים disagree about when spending from the purse counts as מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways the holy coin can get into the purse. It can physically fall in, or the owner can declare that one coin in the purse is הקדש. רבי עקיבא makes the person guilty after the very first coin he spends. The חכמים wait until the whole purse is spent, because only then is it certain that the holy coin was used.

keyTerms.meaning: The smallest coin that has value in halacha; the minimum amount for מעילה
Property that belongs to the Temple
He committed מעילה, meaning he misused Temple property

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two wordings. Here he says 'a פרוטה IN this purse' (בכיס זה). In the next step he says 'a פרוטה FROM this purse' (מן כיס זה). That small difference in wording is what the rest of the sugya is about.

phrases.english: If a consecrated peruta fell
into his purse,
phrases.notes: The purse already had his own ordinary coins in it.

phrases.english: or he said, "A peruta in this purse is consecrated,"
once he spent the first one, he is guilty of misuse,
these are the words of Rabbi Akiva.
And the Sages say:
not until he spends the entire purse.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְלָה פְּרוּטָה שֶׁל הֶקְדֵּשׁ בְּתוֹךְ כִּיסוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה about a consecrated coin mixed into a purse.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, there is מעילה after the first coin is spent. According to the חכמים, there is מעילה only after the whole purse is spent.

steps.title: When רבי עקיבא agrees with the חכמים
steps.stepSummary: If the person said 'a פרוטה FROM this purse is הקדש,' רבי עקיבא agrees that he may keep spending, and there is no מעילה until the whole purse is spent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא agrees with the חכמים when a person says 'a פרוטה from this purse is הקדש.' In that case he may keep spending until he spends the entire purse.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a case where רבי עקיבא agrees with the חכמים. The only change is the wording 'from this purse' instead of 'in this purse.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: With this wording, even רבי עקיבא lets the person keep spending coins. He becomes guilty only when he spends the whole purse. So the argument in the previous step applies only to the 'in this purse' case.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva agrees with the Sages
in the case of one who says, "A peruta from this purse is consecrated,"
that he may keep on spending
until he spends the entire purse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the argument from step 12 by giving a case where רבי עקיבא agrees with the חכמים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When someone says 'a פרוטה from this purse is הקדש,' everyone agrees there is no מעילה until the whole purse is spent.

steps.title: Why the first case is different from the last case
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports that ריש לקיש pointed out a contradiction to רבי יוחנן. Why does רבי עקיבא disagree in the first case of the משנה but agree in the last case?
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: ריש לקיש raised a contradiction to רבי יוחנן. What is different about the first case, and what is different about the last case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It reports a challenge: the two wordings in the משנה ('in this purse' and 'from this purse') seem to mean the same thing, so why does רבי עקיבא rule differently in each?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both cases the person said that one coin in the purse is holy. 'In' and 'from' look like a tiny difference. ריש לקיש wants to know what reason could make רבי עקיבא change his ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised a contradiction (literally, he threw two sources against each other)
The first part of the משנה
The last part of the משנה

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי, אֲמַר:
phrases.english: GEMARA: When Rav Dimi came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: רָמֵי לֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Reish Lakish raised a contradiction to Rabbi Yochanan:
What is different about the first case,
phrases.notes: This is 'a פרוטה IN this purse,' where רבי עקיבא disagrees.

phrases.english: and what is different about the last case?
phrases.notes: This is 'a פרוטה FROM this purse,' where רבי עקיבא agrees.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the difference the משנה draws between steps 12 and 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's different rulings in the first case and the last case of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'A פרוטה in this purse' and 'a פרוטה from this purse' seem to say the same thing, so the ruling should be the same.

steps.title: The last case means the purse will not be left without הקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the last case is about someone who said 'this purse will not be exempt from הקדש.' He meant that the last coin left will be the holy one.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: the last case is talking about someone who says 'this purse will not be exempt from הקדש.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש. He explains that the last case uses a different wording, and that wording has a different meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person did not say that a specific coin is holy right now. He said that the purse will not end up without giving something to הקדש. So he may spend coins freely, and only the last coin is holy. He is guilty only when he spends that last coin too.

keyTerms.meaning: From the obligation to give to הקדש

steps.whatToRemember: In 'a פרוטה in this purse,' רבי עקיבא makes the person guilty of מעילה after the first coin. In the last case, the person meant that the purse will not be left without giving to הקדש. Then only the last coin is holy, so even רבי עקיבא agrees there is no מעילה until the whole purse is spent.

phrases.english: He said to him: The last case
is about one who says, "This purse will not be exempt
from consecration."
phrases.notes: He means he won't use up the whole purse without leaving one coin for the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵיפָא בְּאוֹמֵר לֹא יִפָּטֵור כִּיס זֶה מִן הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the last case has a different meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both wordings mean that one coin in the purse is holy right now.
steps.terutzMaskana: The last case means 'this purse will not be left without giving to הקדש,' so only the final coin is holy.

steps.title: רבין's version: purses versus bulls
steps.stepSummary: According to רבין, ריש לקיש's contradiction was between our purse משנה and a משנה that says the larger of two bulls is the one that becomes הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבין came, he said: ריש לקיש pointed out a contradiction to רבי יוחנן between the purses and the bulls. We learned in a משנה: if someone says 'one of my bulls is הקדש' and he has two bulls, the larger one is הקדש!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of ריש לקיש's challenge. In this version, our purse משנה is compared to a different משנה about bulls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the bulls, we assume the owner meant the better animal, because a person gives to הקדש generously. By that logic, the purse owner who said 'a פרוטה from this purse' should mean the best coin. Then that one coin would be holy and fixed in place, so why may he keep spending until the last coin?

keyTerms.meaning: He pointed out a contradiction to him (he 'threw' one source against another)
Purses, meaning our משנה about a holy coin mixed into a purse
Bulls, meaning the other משנה about consecrating one of his bulls
Consecrated property that belongs to the Temple
The larger of them, because we assume he gave the better one

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new challenge on top of רב דימי's. It is a different report of the same conversation between ריש לקיש and רבי יוחנן, and the challenge is worded differently in it.

phrases.english: When Ravin came, he said:
He raised a contradiction to him: purses against bulls,
phrases.notes: 'He' is ריש לקיש and 'him' is רבי יוחנן, the same pair from step 14.

phrases.english: as we learned in a משנה:
One who says, "One of my bulls is consecrated":
if he had two,
the larger of them is consecrated!
phrases.notes: The exclamation mark shows that this is a challenge. If we assume he meant the best bull, we should also assume he meant the best coin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This is a second report (רבין's) of the challenge that רב דימי reported in step 14. Here the purse case is compared to an outside משנה instead of to another part of the same משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The last case of the purse משנה (step 13), where he may keep spending until the whole purse is used up.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The bulls משנה shows that we assume a person consecrates generously and means the best item. So the purse owner should mean the best coin, which would make one specific coin holy right away.

steps.title: He meant the last coin, not the best coin
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the last case is about someone who said 'this purse will not be exempt from הקדש,' so he meant whichever coin is left at the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: the last case is talking about someone who said, 'This purse will not be exempt from הקדש.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers ריש לקיש's challenge in רבין's version. He uses the same explanation he gave in רב דימי's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The bulls rule only applies when a person picks out one item and means the best one. Here his words show a different intention. He only wanted to make sure the purse is not left with nothing for הקדש, so the holy coin is simply the last one left. That is why he may spend freely until the last coin.

keyTerms.meaning: The last case of the משנה
Will not be exempt from הקדש, meaning something in it must end up holy

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions of the challenge, רב דימי's and רבין's, end with the same answer. In the last case, the man meant that the final coin left in the purse is the holy one. So there is no מעילה until the whole purse is spent, and the 'best item' rule from the bulls does not apply.

phrases.english: He said to him:
The latter clause is where one says:
"This purse will not be exempt from consecration."
phrases.notes: These are the same words as in step 15. He meant that whatever coin remains last is the holy one.

steps.triggerLanguage: סֵיפָא בְּאוֹמֵר לֹא יִפָּטֵור כִּיס זֶה מִן הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 by repeating the case definition from step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the last clause is about a person whose words show what he meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think the purse owner, like the bull owner, meant the best item, so one specific coin would be holy right away.
steps.terutzMaskana: He said 'this purse will not be exempt from הקדש,' which means the last coin left is holy. So he may keep spending until then, and the bulls rule does not apply.
